focus: Section 3.2.1, Scaled Dot-Product Attention. Explain scaled dot-product attention using small, editable Q, K, and V matrices. Show similarity scores, normalized attention weights, and the output. Let the learner edit values and switch scaling on/off. Guide them through equal scores and a dominant score. Check that each row of weights sums to one and that the output equals the weighted sum of V. Do not train a Transformer.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows matrix multiplication and basic probability but has not studied Transformers.

plan.concept: Scaled dot-product attention: scores QK^T/sqrt(d_k), softmax over keys, weighted sum of V.
learning_outcomes: Compute similarity scores between a query and all keys.
Explain why dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps softmax out of saturated regions.
Show that each row of attention weights sums to 1 and the output is the weighted sum of V rows.
plan.visual_strategy: Editable Q, K, V matrices feed a pipeline of scores -> scaled scores -> softmax weights -> output; heatmaps and bars show each stage; a sweep shows how scaling changes weight sharpness as d_k grows.
plan.misconception: Scaling is not a normalization of the output; it only rescales the logits before softmax, changing how peaked the weights are.
